band.cite: docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 'Each side's men under arms': a block's strength is men present, which lies between present for duty (inferred about 100,000 to 165,000) and the rolls (inferred about 145,000 to 245,000); the edges rounded outward per the review nit (95,000; 250,000). No dated 31 July return exists: the note's rule is that a run is not failed below the lower edge. Cross-check on the upper edge (lane 1.11r3): Cameron's speech of 22 June 1861 claims 250,000 men in the field, a public claim and not a return, consistent with the edge; the 1 July report (OR III-1 pp. 303-305) remains the anchor

band.cite: docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 and Appendix B A3: whole Confederacy about 112,040 in July (Livermore p. 42, an estimate he calls probably too low), rounded outward to 100,000; above 32,232 effectives at Bull Run alone (Livermore p. 77). Ceiling 200,000 [I]: docs/research/_leads/T2-strengths.md, section 1, corrected reasoning (R44), Walker to Davis, 24 July 1861, OR IV-1 pp. 496-497. His 190 regiments and 34 battalions give a rough paper estimate of about 200,000 to 210,000 for those units [I], not a count of men present or under arms. The independent companies, twelve recently called regiments and reserve corps of 30,000 are outside that count. The 200,000 ceiling is an inferred, revisable calibration band [I], not an upper bound the sources prove; Davis's 20 July message gives no troop count
